Better Late Than Never: All-New VW T-Roc Is Coming to Australia in Early 2027, Almost Two Years Late
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The second generation of the Volkswagen T-Roc subcompact crossover SUV was introduced in August 2025, but it will probably take almost two years to get to the Land Down Under. Well, at least it wasn’t sacrificed on the altar of business recuperation.
There’s no denying – the second largest global automaker, Volkswagen AG, is going through a rough patch. Just recently we heard that the company stopped the development of the ID. Golf because they can’t “afford it” anymore; wage talks with the workers at home in Germany collapsed in October, and the company might face a strike in January 2027, and Volkswagen, plus Audi and Porsche, continued to lose hard-earned sales in the United States during the third quarter of the year.
Every region and market is now more important than ever, so it’s a good thing that Volkswagen Australia has confirmed that the all-new Volkswagen T-Roc will finally arrive at local dealerships in early 2027, “ushering in the next chapter for one of the brand's most successful nameplates.” The Volkswagen T-Roc was originally introduced globally at the 2017 Frankfurt Motor Show and launched in November 2017, almost a decade ago on the Volkswagen Group MQB A1 platform.
Generally considered the SUV companion of the iconic VW Golf, the T-Roc resides in the small space between the T-Cross and the Tiguan, with the second iteration launched in August 2025 based on the premium MQB Evo platform shared with the Golf Mk8.5, among others. According to VW Australia, the “next-generation model builds on the strengths that have made the T-Roc a customer favourite, introducing mild-hybrid technology, a more sophisticated design and significant advances in technology, safety and comfort.”
Volkswagen’s newest styling language and enhanced lighting signatures underpin the fresh exterior, and inside customers will discover an upgraded cabin with Volkswagen's latest-generation digital technologies. The T-Roc range comes with mild hybrid technology for the first time in Australia, but the new model also comes with more interior space and additional practical features.
There is also Volkswagen's latest infotainment system, a new generation of driver assistance technologies and a big range of comfort-focused features. However, additional information, including local pricing, model specifications, as well as Australian equipment details, will be announced at a later date closer to the market arrival.
Currently, the global model features both front-wheel drive and all-wheel drive setups and is powered by the company’s ubiquitous 1.5-liter TSI gasoline engine and a seven-speed DSG transmission with mild hybrid 48-volt assistance. Most likely the Australian model will mirror this setup when it goes on sale in the market sometime next year.
“Our Volkswagen T-Roc has become one of Volkswagen Australia's most successful and popular models, resonating strongly with customers looking for a compact SUV with genuine character, style and everyday versatility. The all-new generation builds on the qualities that have made the T-Roc such a success in Australia, while delivering meaningful advances in design, technology, comfort, safety and efficiency,” said Piergiorgio Minto, Brand Director of Volkswagen Passenger Vehicles.
